corpus.note: Real Typesense (not the SQLite proxy). Single-node local laptop instance — production hardware has more headroom. Corpus accumulated across seed runs so keyword selectivity is mixed (some terms 0 hits, some ~426k), making the broad-term tail heavier than a clean synthetic distribution — a conservative measurement.

tuning_experiment.lever: search_cutoff_ms (Typesense returns best-ranked-so-far once query exceeds the budget)
tuning_experiment.conclusion: search_cutoff_ms=150 wins the text-search gate decisively (keyword p95 555->164). num_typos=1 adds nothing and worsens p99, so NOT adopted. Empty q=* 'browse all 1.1M newest' is a list not a search: cutoff helps (579->471) but cannot reach <200ms because the cost is faceting+sorting the whole corpus — tracked separately (opt-in faceting for empty queries).

end_to_end_searchservice.note: Through the real eden.observability.SearchService.search() with the shipped change (typesense_search_cutoff_ms=150), full production param set, wall-clock incl. Python+aiohttp overhead.

shipped_change.wiring: src/eden/observability/search_service.py: adds search_cutoff_ms to Typesense search params when > 0

honest_caveats: Single-node laptop Typesense, not staging hardware — treat absolute ms as conservative.

search_cutoff_ms trades exhaustiveness for bounded latency: broad low-selectivity queries may return fewer than all matches, ranked best-first. Selective queries (the common case) complete well under the budget, unaffected.
Empty-query browse-all (q=*) is above the gate and is a separate follow-up (opt-in faceting), not a text-search regression.
